title: Understanding Proper Drainage Slope and Waste Velocity
description: Achieving proper drainage flow depends on maintaining correct pipe pitch throughout horizontal DWV runs. A common misconception is that steeper slopes always drain better. In reality, an excessive slope can allow liquid waste to flow rapidly past solid waste, leaving dry debris behind to cause persistent blockages. Conversely, an insufficient slope allows water to pool, creating slow drains and sediment buildup. Professional plumbers rely on accurate torpedo levels to set uniform fall according to local plumbing codes. Always consult your jurisdiction's governing code to verify the exact required drop per foot based on pipe diameter.

Understanding Proper Drainage Slope and Waste Velocity

Achieving proper drainage flow depends on maintaining correct pipe pitch throughout horizontal DWV runs. A common misconception is that steeper slopes always drain better. In reality, an excessive slope can allow liquid waste to flow rapidly past solid waste, leaving dry debris behind to cause persistent blockages. Conversely, an insufficient slope allows water to pool, creating slow drains and sediment buildup. Professional plumbers rely on accurate torpedo levels to set uniform fall according to local plumbing codes. Always consult your jurisdiction's governing code to verify the exact required drop per foot based on pipe diameter.
